must_remember: Secondary cells act as galvanic cells during discharge and as electrolytic cells during charging due to the reversibility of their chemical reactions.
In a fully charged lead-acid accumulator, the positive plate is $PbO_2$ and the negative plate is spongy $Pb$, immersed in an aqueous $H_2SO_4$ solution.
The terminal voltage during discharge is given by $V = E - Ir$, while during charging it is $V = E + Ir$.
Internal resistance of secondary cells is extremely low, enabling them to deliver very high surge currents.
Ampere-hour (Ah) efficiency of lead-acid cells typically ranges from $80\%$ to $90\%$, and energy efficiency is always lower than Ah efficiency.

glossary.meaning: An electrochemical cell that can be electrically recharged after discharge by passing current in the reverse direction.
A storage battery, most commonly the lead-acid type, used to store electrical energy in chemical form.
The ratio of the product of discharge current and time to the product of charging current and time, expressed as a percentage.
The opposition offered by the electrolyte and electrodes of a cell to the flow of electric current, measured in ohms ($\Omega$).
